title: Pause and resume a repo's intake

story.as_a: Mark in fleet_dash, or a session that sees a repo flooding the loop
story.i_want_to: pause a repo's intake and resume it later
story.so_that: new issues stop costing triage while the work already in flight carries on, and nothing reported is lost

rationale: PRD R4 lists 'pause or resume a repo's intake' among the intervention verbs. The only switch today is DISPATCH_DRIVER_ENABLED (dispatch_driver.ex:254), which is global and stops in-flight placement too, and revoking the intake source (Intake.revoke_source/3, intake.ex:1263) cuts the webhook so reports are lost. A pause is a per-source fact the triage path reads: the webhook keeps recording, and promotion and triage dispatch skip the source until it resumes.

acceptance_criteria.description: intake_sources gains paused_at (utc_datetime_usec, nullable) and paused_reason (text, at most 1000 codepoints, nullable), set only by Intake.set_paused/4 and Intake.clear_paused/3, never cast by create_changeset/2 or update_source/4.
While a source is paused, TriageTriggerWorker.candidates/1 skips its pending_triage records, which stay pending_triage, so they promote on the first run after resume.

While a source is paused, triage@1's candidate predicates include :intake_not_paused, so TriageDispatcher.candidates/1 returns none of its stories at detected; stories already past detected are placed, worked and merged as before.
The GitHub webhook for a paused source still verifies, records the delivery and applies it to the intake record (Intake.receive_github_delivery/2 is unchanged), so no report is lost while paused.

POST /api/v1/projects/:id/intake/pause (reason and intervention_id required) and /resume (intervention_id required) are role: :agent and RequireHumanAnchor; they act on the project's one live source (Intake.source_for_project/2), answer the source's public fields plus paused_at and paused_reason, and are 404 no_intake_source for a project with none or another tenant's project.

Pausing a paused source or resuming a running one answers 200 with the source unchanged and writes nothing; each real change appends one audit chain entry, intake_paused or intake_resumed, naming the actor and the reason, and a retry with the same intervention_id writes no second entry.
Each project row of factory_overview carries intake_paused_at, nil when running.

MCP tools intake_pause and intake_resume call the routes with project_id, reason and an intervention_id (generated when absent), have mcp-server/README.md rows and a wiring test; their descriptions say a pause stops promotion and triage only, never in-flight work or the webhook.

test_cases.name: the pause fields are not castable (unit)
steps: create and update with paused_at and paused_reason in attrs

test_cases.name: a paused source keeps recording and promotes nothing until resume (DataCase)
preconditions: fixture(:intake_source) paused; a signed issues.opened delivery body
expected_results: record pending_triage and no story; then a story at detected

test_cases.name: triage skips a paused project; in-flight work is untouched (DataCase)
preconditions: paused source; one story at detected and one at queued under it; an unpaused second project with a detected story
expected_results: only the second project's story for triage; the queued story is still a driver candidate

test_cases.name: routes, roles and 404s (ConnCase)
preconditions: holder agent key and user key in tenant A; a project with no source; tenant B's project

test_cases.name: idempotent pause and resume, one chain entry per change (DataCase)
preconditions: a running source; a fixed intervention_id
steps: set_paused twice with the same id
expected_results: one intake_paused and one intake_resumed entry

test_cases.name: the overview names a paused project (DataCase)
preconditions: a paused and a running project
expected_results: the paused project's row carries its intake_paused_at
the running project's row carries intake_paused_at nil

test_cases.name: intake_pause and intake_resume wiring (node --test)
preconditions: mcp-server tool list; stub apiCall and uuidv4

technical_notes: Source schema: lib/loopctl/intake/source.ex:114-158; add the two fields beside revoked_at (:158). Writers mirror update_source/4's chain-entry-per-change pattern (lib/loopctl/intake.ex:618, append_update at :763), on AdminRepo with the explicit tenant_id predicate the module uses.

Why not PATCH /intake/sources/:id: IntakeSourceController is role: :user (lib/loopctl_web/controllers/intake_source_controller.ex:46) and @updatable_fields (intake.ex:600) are configuration; a pause is an intervention open to holders (PRD R4), so it is its own pair of writers and routes, and the source row stays the one record of the fact.
Promotion: TriageTriggerWorker.candidates/1 (lib/loopctl/workers/triage_trigger_worker.ex:359) adds a join on intake_sources with paused_at IS NULL.

Triage: add :intake_not_paused to Loopctl.Agents.Candidates (lib/loopctl/agents/candidates.ex, beside :single_active_source at :365, which it requires) and to triage@1's predicate list (lib/loopctl/agents/specs/triage_v1.ex).
Webhook: Intake.receive_github_delivery/2 (intake.ex:1524) authenticates on active_source/1, which reads revoked_at, not paused_at; it is untouched.
Idempotency: the intervention_id is stored in the chain entry's metadata and checked before the write under the source row lock (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE).
Overview: Overview.for_tenant/2 is provided by US-52.30.
Routes in lib/loopctl_web/router.ex beside /projects/:id/progress (:527); MCP in lib/factory.js (US-52.30) plus declarations and cases in mcp-server/index.js; CHANGELOG.md lists the routes.
non_goals: Pausing placement or merges of in-flight work: DISPATCH_DRIVER_ENABLED remains the fleet-wide switch.
The intake re-check skipping a paused source: US-52.36 adds its own predicate.
Revoking or re-enrolling a source: unchanged (Intake.revoke_source/3).

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.33.6: a client that loses the answer retries with the same intervention_id and writes nothing new.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.33.1: the pause lives on the intake_sources row in Postgres and is read by both the promotion and the triage query, so a restart or deploy keeps it; AC-52.33.4: deliveries keep landing on intake records meanwhile.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.33.6: pausing twice changes nothing and appends no second chain entry.
failure_modes.slow: n/a: no network call; two row writes inside one request.
failure_modes.reach: AC-52.33.2: the paused records are picked up by the existing minute cron on its first run after resume; nothing else has to be found or restarted.

definition_of_done: On production, intake_pause on the loopctl-e2e-sandbox project, then a new sandbox issue, leaves its record pending_triage; intake_resume promotes it within two minutes.
The audit chain shows intake_paused and intake_resumed entries naming the session's holder.
defaults: A pause stops promotion and triage dispatch only; placement and merges of items past detected continue.
